verdict.rationale: Appwrite's own Docker-based self-hosting runs the full Appwrite stack on any machine with a Docker CLI. The docs name a self-hosted full local instance as a test path, Functions advertise 'Develop locally, deploy when ready', and the CLI can target a self-hosted endpoint. A community user also praised the containerized setup for offline development and testing. However, the local route is the general self-hosting install, not a purpose-built local emulator or CLI dev workflow, so only part of the story is documented. missing for 10: a dedicated local emulator or CLI 'start local stack' command, documented local-to-cloud promotion workflow, hands-on corroboration of full-stack local development parity.

support.subject: As a developer, I can run the whole backend stack locally with an emulator or CLI before deploying

citations.quote: You can install and run Appwrite on any operating system that can run a Docker CLI.
13+ runtimes. Develop locally, deploy when ready.
Add the --endpoint flag if you're using a self-hosted instance of Appwrite.
They liked that Appwrite provides a containerized setup, which should make distributed development and testing easier.
